args.title: checkout-api rollback to v2.3.0 due to failed health checks
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to all production regions and was failing health checks (error rate 0.18, healthy=false in us-east, us-west, eu-west). Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The initial rollback attempt partially failed (rollout halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1); a retry completed the rollout to all three regions. Post-rollback status: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. No approval was required since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 regression and the orchestrator error encountered during the first rollback attempt before attempting redeploy.

trace.final:
The timeout was a false alarm — the incident was created successfully (INC-0001), so no retry was needed.

## Summary

**Root cause:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions — `healthy: false` with an 18% error rate (0.18) across us-east, us-west, and eu-west.

**Rollback:** Rolled back to **v2.3.0**, the most recent release with `status: healthy` in production (v2.2.9 was older; v2.3.1-rc was never a production release).
- **First attempt partially failed:** the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-west and eu-west on the unhealthy v2.3.1. I verified state per-region rather than assuming success.
- **Retry succeeded:** all three regions now on v2.3.0, `status: rolled_out`.

**Verified recovery:** `healthy: true`, error rate down from 0.18 → 0.002, all regions on v2.3.0.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on checkout-api, documenting the failing version, the rollback target and rationale, the partial-failure/retry sequence, and post-rollback metrics.

No change-manager approval was required — v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production.

**Two items worth follow-up:**
1. The **orchestrator error** during the first rollback attempt is a tooling reliability issue that could bite us during a real incident when every minute counts. The retry worked, but this should be investigated.
2. The **v2.3.1 regression** itself is unexplained — I have not diagnosed why it failed, only reverted it. It should not be redeployed until that's understood.

Note that I left the incident's follow-up items in the summary rather than attempting any diagnosis, since the task was to restore service and report — let me know if you'd like me to dig into the v2.3.1 failure or the orchestrator error next.
